page: Microsoft Azure M16bs_v3 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at base speeds up to 4.0 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. Compute resources are paired with a 105 MB Level-3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX-INT8, and AMX-TILE. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core). The instance includes zero bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPU accelerators, utilizing remote block storage for persistent data needs.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread throughput alongside predictable multi-core capacity. Single-core evaluations reflect elevated scores, including a Geekbench single-core score of 2213.0 and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 32.93 GB/sec. Large uncached memory bandwidth sustains 108.38 GB/sec in read routines and 67.71 GB/sec in write operations, while small cached block reads achieve 1383.1 GB/sec. In distributed key-value benchmarks, the server delivers 22.5 million operations per second in Redis SET routines. In addition, hardware-accelerated integer extensions yield top-tier inference speeds during text generation with smaller 135M language models, registering 333.36 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, the M16bs_v3 balances high memory density with standard compute density, offering an efficient profile for memory-bound tasks that do not require proportional GPU or dense local disk arrays. The absence of local temporary or ephemeral NVMe solid-state storage requires architectural consideration, as all disk input/output relies on attached network volumes. The combination of ample RAM per vCPU, strong single-core responsiveness, and advanced matrix extensions makes this instance type effective for relational database management systems, distributed in-memory caching tiers, intermediate ETL workflows, and memory-constrained analytical applications.
description: Microsoft Azure M16bs_v3 is a memory-optimized instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, engineered for memory-intensive enterprise tasks. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor clocking up to 4.0 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, backed by 105 MB of L3 cache and advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX. The M16bs_v3 includes no bundled local disk storage and no GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for data persistence. Benchmark results indicate strong single-core compute performance and high memory bandwidth, alongside dependable multi-core throughput. This platform is suited for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, and large-footprint analytical workloads.
